name: Neural Tide
tagline: Kadalthira's AI and ML club. Read the paper, train the model, ship the demo.
about:
Neural Tide is the AI and machine learning club of Kadalthira Institute of Technology, a campus close enough to the sea at Vettucaud that you can hear the waves from the third-floor lab. Four second-year students started it in 2022 to read one paper a week together. It now has around two hundred active members from every department, and a GPU workstation we fought very hard for.

Our year runs on three tracks. Foundations is for first-years and anyone switching in: Python, linear algebra without fear, and the first neural network you write by hand. Builders take on a semester-long project in small teams, and many of those projects are about Malayalam and Kerala: speech recognition for fishing-boat radio, a reader for handwritten ration-card forms, crop-disease detection from phone photos. Paper Club meets on Wednesday evenings to argue about whatever came out that week.

We're student-run and faculty-mentored, and nearly everything we do is open to students from other colleges. If you're not from Kadalthira, come to a Paper Club session anyway. Nobody will ask for your ID card.

events.name: Neural Nets by Hand

venue.name: Seminar Hall 2, Kadalthira Institute of Technology

events.about:
Our Foundations opener for the new batch. Before anyone touches a framework, we build a tiny neural network with pen, paper and a calculator: three inputs, one hidden layer, and enough arithmetic to see exactly what a weight is and why it moves. Then we write the same network in thirty lines of Python and watch it learn to tell ripe bananas from raw ones in a dataset we photographed at the Chalai market.

It's designed for first-years and anyone from a non-CS branch who keeps hearing the word 'gradient' and nodding politely. By the end you'll have trained your first model and, more importantly, you'll know what happened inside it.
events.guidelines: Bring a pen, a notebook and a calculator; a laptop helps for the second half but you can share. We'll send a notebook link the evening before, so you can run it on a free cloud notebook if your laptop is slow. Please be seated by 1:50; the hall doors close at 2:15 for the hand-calculation part.

events.name: Tide Hack 2026: Models for Malayalam

venue.name: Main Block, Kadalthira Institute of Technology

events.about:
Twenty-four hours to build something useful for people who speak Malayalam. Teams of two to four picked one of three tracks: speech (voice notes, radio, phone calls), text (forms, handwriting, news) or vision (signboards, labels, crops). Ezhuthani Language Labs opened up three cleaned datasets just for the weekend, and Mazhanila Analytics gave every team GPU credits.

Thirty-eight teams came from eleven colleges. The winning team built a tool that turns a fisherman's spoken catch report into the cooperative's daily register; second place read prices off handwritten vegetable-shop boards in Chalai and Palayam. The fee covered four meals, the night snacks and the T-shirt.
events.guidelines: Teams of two to four; register each member separately and use the same team name. Bring your college ID and a laptop. Pre-trained models are allowed and encouraged, but the datasets released on the day must be part of your solution. Sleeping is permitted in the reading room after midnight. Judging is on usefulness first, then technical depth, then the demo.

events.name: Paper Club Live: Small Models, Big Ideas

venue.name: Library Auditorium, Kadalthira Institute of Technology

events.about:
Once a semester, Paper Club leaves its usual classroom and invites someone who writes the papers we read. This time, Dr. Lekha Ramanathan talked about making language models small enough to run on a phone that costs under ₹8,000: distillation, quantisation, and the unglamorous work of deciding what a model is allowed to forget.

She walked through her group's recent work on a compact Malayalam-English model, including the results that didn't work, and then took questions for forty minutes. Students from four colleges came, and the discussion carried on at the tea shop outside the gate for a good while after the hall closed.
events.guidelines: Open to everyone; outside students should carry any photo ID for the gate. The session is in English, with questions welcome in Malayalam. Please read the one-page summary we post two days before, so the Q&A goes deeper.

events.name: Datasets from Home: Malayalam Speech Sprint

venue.name: Language Lab, Kadalthira Institute of Technology

events.about:
Good Malayalam speech models need voices from Kasaragod to Parassala, and most open datasets sound like they were all recorded in one city. This Saturday we build a better one together. You'll record a few hundred short sentences in your own accent, then learn how to check and label other people's recordings so the data is actually usable.

Sruthi from Ezhuthani Language Labs will explain consent, licences and why every clip needs a speaker card, and Ameen will show how we store and version the data on the club workstation. Everything collected goes into an openly licensed dataset with every contributor credited.
events.guidelines: Bring earphones with a microphone if you have them; we have twenty spare headsets. Recording is in quiet booths, ten minutes at a time. You'll sign a simple consent form, and you can withdraw your recordings later. Speakers of every dialect are welcome, including people who mix in English the way most of us do.

events.name: Neural Tide Demo Day

venue.name: Central Courtyard, Kadalthira Institute of Technology

events.about:
Eleven Builders teams show what they made this semester, on tables around the courtyard, to anyone who wants to try them. Talk to a model that understands fishing-boat radio chatter, photograph a diseased banana leaf and get a diagnosis, or watch a handwritten ration-card form turn into a spreadsheet row.

A small jury of alumni and industry guests will pick two projects for a summer of mentoring, but the main audience is you: parents, juniors, faculty and anyone curious. Come with questions, and come with a phone so you can try the demos yourself.
events.guidelines: Free and open to the public; outside visitors should carry a photo ID. Demos run from 3:30 to 6:00, so come and go as you like. Please don't upload photos of other people's screens before the teams publish their work.

speakers.name: Prof. Deepa Narayanan
speakers.bio: Has guided Builders projects since the club's first year and insists every team writes down who their user is before any code.

speakers.name: Arjun Kesavan
speakers.bio: Kadalthira alumnus who ships crop advisory tools to farmers in Palakkad and Wayanad, and judges demos by how fast they load on a bad network.
